cells.ask: Tell one person what this stretch of uncertainty has been holding for you, and say in the same breath that you don't know what comes next.
cells.core:
You can say what's true about a situation you don't have the shape of yet. A friendship, a decision, a run of work that hasn't resolved — you feel where it stands, and you move before it's finished instead of waiting for the ending to make it safe to feel.

Not a conclusion you arrived at. A way of holding what's real while it's still open. That's what you can pass on, to someone in the middle of their own unfinished thing or to your own next step: say the feeling and the missing ending at the same time, and notice what surfaces when you do.

cells.tense: You're out ahead of this, bracing for an ending you can't write in yet.
cells.ask: Draw one line for what's true today — one sentence on paper — and let everything past it stay open.
cells.core:
You want the ending visible before you take the step. Feeling your way through something open works, but right now you're living past the open stretch instead of in it — rehearsing the resolution, replaying how it should land, pushing for a shape that doesn't exist yet. The bracing is spending what the feeling needs.

Enough light for the next step is enough. Pick one thing that's true right now and draw your line there — not a plan, not a prediction, one sentence. Where there's real truth in front of you, deciding what's yours keeps the feeling whole instead of stretched toward an ending you can't reach.

cells.tense: You're still over by a door that's behind you now, reading what's past instead of what's here.
cells.ask: Write one unfinished thing down as it stands today — one sentence — and let the sentence end it, not you.
cells.core:
You can feel where something stands, finished or not, and say so. That's quiet here. What's loud is the looking back — at how a thing ended, at the shape it had when it was whole, at what you'd say if you said it. Each look promises the end of the question and delivers another lap around it.

A first move doesn't need a plan. One sentence on paper about where it stands today — no finish, no explanation. Write it and stop there. A small opening can carry more than a finished answer, and it's here the feeling starts moving again.

cells.tense: You're calling this stretch of uncertainty something you're waiting on, but the wait is a reading you keep taking.
cells.ask: Say one wish out loud in your own words, plainly, without explaining it.
cells.core:
You already feel where things stand — you read the room, you know what's true before it settles — but the account you give is that you're still waiting for clarity. The reading is running; you're calling it patience and living off the answers even while calling them pending. What's yours hasn't been claimed.

Moving through what isn't shown doesn't mean fixing a shape onto it; it means feeling what's there until a step shows itself. Say one wish in your own voice, plainly, without laying out how you got there. What surfaces from that is already on its way, and the saying of it is how you find out what you actually want.
